title: A list of bytes crosses the guest boundary as one wasmtime `Val` per byte for the pdf, intl and spreadsheet worlds.
text: `convert` lowers `Value::Bytes` to a `Val::List` of `Val::U8` and lifts it back the same way, because the call bridge calls those exports through wasmtime's dynamic `Func::call_async`. Each byte costs a whole `Val` on the host, so a crossing costs tens of nanoseconds per byte. The image world (`wit/image.wit`) is already called typed: `crates/nvs-ext/src/typed.rs` converts a `Value` to the types `bindgen!` writes for it, so its bytes make one copy each way, and `tests/builtin.rs`'s `a_built_in_call_charges_its_bytes_once_and_not_one_val_per_byte` pins it. The decided fix for the rest is the same: one module under `crates/nvs-ext/src/typed/` per first-party world (`wit/pdf.wit`, `wit/intl.wit`, `wit/spreadsheet.wit`), with its records, enums, variants and methods listed for the `typed` macros. The WIT does not change, and a third-party export stays on the dynamic path. A typed path for flat signatures only was declined because it leaves records that carry bytes per byte, and flattening the worlds because it shapes the API to suit the bridge.
